To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
vector graphics are a useful data format for image recognition and can be leveraged to improve recognition accuracy and efficiency.
vector graphics can be used to recognize objects without rasterization.

(1) we propose an efficient CNN-Free pipeline for object detection in vector graphics, which does not rasterize vector graphics; (2) we build multi-graphs from vector graphics to capture structural information; (3) a dual-stream graph network is designed for vector graphic recognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following contributions.
a novel approach for object detection in graphic documents.
the following three questions:  1. How to efficiently represent vector graphics for object detection and classification.

the proposed method is an efficient and effective method for recognizing vector graphics, which is able to leverage the merits of the vector graphics and achieve superior performances over rasterization-based methods.
the authors propose an efficient CNN free pipeline that does not rasterize the vector graphics and takes the text document as input.
our work explores the potential of using vector graphics as a new input modality in image recognition.

we are the first to explore the vector graphics format in object recognition.
, we are the first to explore the vector graphic format for image recognition tasks.
we are the first to recognize objects in vector graphics without rasterizing them into pixels.

vector graphics are a promising format to recognize visual content.
